summary: Join our comprehensive training on Risk Mapping and Geospatial Technologies for Disaster Management. Equip yourself with essential skills for effective response
lede: Geospatial risk mapping helps disaster management professionals see where hazards, exposed people and assets, and vulnerabilities overlap. For professionals who shape disaster-risk, resilience, or emergency decisions, the course shows how to interpret hazard and vulnerability maps, apply basic spatial analysis, and work with GIS teams. Participants learn to use map-based evidence in preparedness and emergency planning, including choices about priorities and contingency actions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who regularly make or influence decisions about disaster risk, resilience, and emergency operations. It caters to those in roles where understanding and applying geospatial data is critical to effective disaster management.
audience: Disaster risk reduction (DRR) and resilience officers
Emergency management and civil protection professionals
Public sector planners and policy officers
Private sector risk, security, and business continuity
modules: Foundations of Disaster Risk and Geospatial Thinking
Core Concepts in GIS and Geospatial Data for Disaster Management
Hazard Mapping: Floods, Droughts, Landslides, and Beyond
Building Integrated Risk Maps and Indices
Remote Sensing and Satellite Imagery for Disaster Management
Early Warning, Scenario Modeling, and Contingency Planning
Field Data Collection and Community Mapping
Communicating Risk Through Maps, Dashboards, and Storytelling
Implementing Geospatial Workflows in Your Organization
prerequisites: Participants are expected to have a basic understanding of disaster management and an interest in applying geospatial technologies. No prior GIS experience is required, but familiarity with spatial data concepts will be beneficial.
